args.prompt: Photorealistic vertical photograph, a still frame from professional basketball game footage. An indoor professional arena: polished hardwood floor with a painted lane and free-throw line, a glass backboard with an orange rim and a white net, bright even court lighting, dark empty stands. The camera is on a tripod a few metres behind the ball handler and a little to his right, at about head height, looking down the court toward the basket; the backboard, rim and net are near the top of the frame and fully visible. The two players are anatomically accurate human skeletons made of real ivory bone, with complete, correct anatomy: skull with jaw and teeth, neck vertebrae, rib cage with twelve pairs of ribs and a sternum, clavicles and shoulder blades, spine, pelvis, thigh bones, kneecaps, shin bones, ankle and foot bones, upper arm and forearm bones, and every bone of both hands. The ball handler is in the foreground, seen from behind at three-quarters: he wears white basketball shoes and a white wristband, stands at the top of the key facing the basket and holds a real orange basketball at his right hip in triple threat. His defender wears red basketball shoes and a red wristband: he faces him and the camera a stride and a half in front of him, between him and the basket, in a low, wide defensive stance with his arms out. Both skeletons have the posture and balance of elite athletes and are completely in frame from skull to feet. The frame has some dark arena above the backboard at the top and some empty hardwood below the ball handler's feet at the bottom. No skin, no muscle, no clothing except the shoes and wristbands. No other people, no logos, no text, no watermark. Sharp focus, natural colour, a real photograph.

One continuous shot from a locked-off tripod camera behind the ball handler: the camera never moves, pans, tilts or zooms. Two anatomically accurate human skeletons play one-on-one basketball at real professional game speed, with real weight, balance and body mechanics. Every bone keeps its exact shape, size and place for the whole clip: nothing bends, stretches, morphs, merges, multiplies or disappears, and each skeleton always has one skull, two arms, two hands, two legs and its own shoes. The ball handler in white shoes starts a live dribble with his right hand, sizing up his man. At about two seconds he makes one hard in-and-out dribble: he pushes the ball out hard to his right as if to drive, then snatches it straight back with the same hand. The defender in red shoes bites: he opens his hips and takes a big step toward the drive, his weight going the wrong way. In that instant the ball handler gathers and rises straight up into a smooth, balanced pull-up jump shot: full extension, high release, follow-through. The defender is too late to recover and contest. The ball arcs high and drops cleanly through the net, a swish. The shooter lands balanced and holds his follow-through. Natural footwork, realistic acceleration and real ball physics. No slow motion, no cuts, no text. Sound: only the ball on the hardwood, sneaker squeaks and the swish of the net; no voices, no crowd, no music.

The ball handler in white shoes dribbles with his right hand and makes one hard in-and-out dribble: the ball pushed out to his right, then snatched straight back. This time the defender in red shoes does not bite: he stays square and balanced, hips square, with one short slide. Immediately the ball handler explodes off his back foot: one hard, low dribble straight at the defender's hip, his shoulder into the defender's hip in a solid bump, and he is past him, attacking the basket: two long steps and a right-handed layup off the glass that goes in. The defender is knocked off balance, turns and trails the play. Natural footwork, realistic acceleration, contact and real ball physics. No slow motion, no cuts, no text. Sound: only the ball on the hardwood, sneaker squeaks, the bump and the ball off the glass; no voices, no crowd, no music.
